description: A sequencer built from four nodes: time runs outward from each node to the particles connected to it, firing a trigger and a pitch as it reaches each one

params.text: Sets the tempo of all four nodes, 15 to 240 bpm
Turns all four nodes on and off
Turns the random drifting of the nodes around the display on and off
Sets how fast the nodes drift as two to the power of its setting, a sixteenth of full speed at -4 and double at +1
Sets the root note that the pitches are quantised to
Picks the scale the pitches are quantised to, among them the Messiaen modes of limited transposition and the seventh chords
Chooses whether a particle's pitch comes from its radius, small particles sounding higher, or from its height in the display
Removes every particle from the display
Turns that coloured node on and off
Shifts the pitch of that coloured node by up to five octaves either way

inputs.text: A trigger turns all four nodes on and off
Adds 5 bpm per volt to the tempo set by the BPM knob
A trigger turns the random drifting of the nodes on and off
Sets the root note from a pitch voltage, twelve semitones to the volt, in place of the root note knob

outputs.text: Fires a 10V pulse for every particle of all four nodes, stealing voices when more particles sound than there are polyphonic channels
Carries the quantised pitch of the particles of all four nodes, stealing voices when more sound than there are polyphonic channels
Fires a 10V pulse as that node's time reaches each of its particles, one polyphonic channel per particle
Carries the quantised pitch of each particle on that node, one polyphonic channel per particle

notes: click a node to drag it, and click elsewhere to add a particle; dragging a particle out of the display removes it
the display comes up empty and the nodes reach nothing: click in the display to add particles before anything is fired.
menu: Play mode — continuous or 1-shot, which changes what the PLAY button and the PLAY input do
Collisions — whether the four nodes bounce off one another as they drift
Polyphony channels — sets how many particles each node can sound at once, Monophonic or 1 to 16
